rv.q: If you think that “wiping away tears of laughter and sorrow” is one those activities that, like “rolling in the aisles”, only happens in reviews, you give should this show a visit.
This joyous, cathartic musical looks set to see out many calendars.
The Girls is a superb night in the theatre.
With all the arguments and upheaval currently in the world, The Girls is a heart warming tonic.
Yet The Girls also blossoms into a feel-good hit as bright as a field of sunflowers.
The music is so good that the thinness of the plot, albeit based on a moving true story, can be forgotten, a large number of jokes helping to warm up the audience along the way.
It makes me so sad to think it will only be on for a few more weeks when it is, really and truly, one of the best things I have ever seen in the West end.
The Girls is simply joyous and an exhilarating triumph.
I can’t think of a time recently when I’ve laughed and cried so much in an evening, and if not for that, what is theatre for?

It's not a complicated story but it is full of surprising people played with a raw truthfulness, its humour and emotion heightened by delightful music and a final burst of sunshine that sends audiences home both moved and very happy.
Gary Barlow and Tim Firth's new musical – based on the 2003 film Calendar Girls, is a delight to behold.
All in all it is an enjoyable watch.
The Girls is one of the best British musicals I’ve seen in years.
The Girls is a finely polished production, a high quality home-made British offering with a heart-warming true story and a fine score.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this warm, feel-good musical adaptation of Calendar Girls, praising Barlow's score and the strong female ensemble. A crowd-pleasing hit with genuine emotional depth.
